mood.summary: All eyes are on the July PCE inflation data at 08:30 ET and NVIDIA's earnings after the bell; the market is in a holding pattern until these major catalysts are released.

traderLens.name: Minervini
traderLens.view: Market is in a holding pattern. Not an ideal environment for new breakouts until key data is released. Focus on managing existing positions.

traderLens.name: Ted Zhang
traderLens.view: Rotation back into tech yesterday was tentative. NVDA's report will determine if institutional flow commits to the sector or rotates out.

traderLens.name: Clement Ang
traderLens.view: This is a C/D-grade environment until PCE and NVDA are out of the way. No new entries. The risk of a gap down on bad news is elevated.

traderLens.name: SRxTrades
traderLens.view: Pre-market action is dominated by earnings reactions. PLAB shows a clean gap up on volume, while INTU shows a clean gap down. Wait for setups to form after the open.

traderLens.name: Jeff
traderLens.view: Today is about discipline. Do not trade based on predictions about PCE or NVDA. React to the price action, don't anticipate it. Stick to your stops.

traderLens.name: Qullamaggie
traderLens.view: The main catalyst is NVDA AMC. A strong beat and raise could ignite momentum across the semiconductor and AI space. An earnings miss could kill the recent rally.

traderLens.name: Composite
traderLens.view: Stay on the sidelines until after the PCE data at 8:30 ET. The reaction to that number will set the morning tone. Do not initiate new swing positions before NVDA reports. The risk of an overnight gap against you is too high.

news.headline: Stock futures are mixed as investors brace for crucial PCE inflation data and Nvidia's highly-anticipated earnings report.
Intuit (INTU) shares plunge pre-market after company issues weak forward guidance for fiscal 2027, citing pricing pressures.
Photronics (PLAB) soars in pre-market after reporting Q3 earnings and revenue that beat analyst expectations.
Crude oil prices extend losses on signs of easing Middle East tensions and hopes the Strait of Hormuz could reopen.
10-Year Treasury yield holds steady around 4.63% after easing in the previous session.
